## TL;DR

I built the macOS Hub with `xcodebuild` into a DerivedData folder outside the repo, ran its 188-case XCTest suite (all pass), launched the app, and drove it through empty state, server discovery, add, and the connected web view. Everything I could reach works, and I found no crash, blank screen, or broken screen to fix, so this pass makes no source change. It adds the QA record `docs/qa/2026-11-macos-hub-qa.md`. The gap is the logged-in projects and tasks screens: my sign-in attempt never reached the email field, so that check is open and needs a person.

## Work and rationale

The task asks for three things: build and launch with window-only screenshots, fix whatever breaks, and record the findings. I built first because a green build plus a green unit suite rules out the most common failure. The build succeeded on the first try, and the test target passed 188 cases with zero failures, so the unit layer is not the problem.

For the launch I used the README's isolated-registry recipe with `REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY` pointed at a scratch folder, so the QA run never touched the real Hub registry. Launching the binary directly from a shell produced a live process with no visible window. Launching the same bundle through `open -n --env …` produced the expected window. I recorded this as a launch-path difference rather than a Hub bug, because the app did not crash and LaunchServices is how a user starts it. I did not dig further.

Captures used `screencapture -l<windowid>` against the Hub window only. The first capture hit the menu bar because I had picked the wrong window ID, so I checked the PID and bounds before reusing the helper. Every screenshot in this run is window-only.

Discovery worked end to end. The Add server sheet listed `repoos` at `localhost:7171`, coming from the live server. Clicking its `+` filled the URL field, and the Add server button ran the health check and wrote the entry to the isolated `servers.json` with `lastHealth: healthy`. The sidebar then showed the row, and the connected pane rendered the server's sign-in page inside the isolated web view.

I then tried to sign in with the documented dev login for the bootstrap admin, so I could reach the projects and tasks screens. The email never landed in the field. Two attempts with synthetic clicks and keystrokes produced no input, and I did not find a reliable way to focus the web view from here. I stopped there rather than keep guessing coordinates. The logged-in screens are the largest unverified part of the acceptance criteria, and the QA record lists them as open.

## Approaches tried

- Building with the repo's README recipe, then running the suite with `xcodebuild test`. Both passed, so I did not need to touch any source.
- Launching the binary directly. It produced a process with no window, so I switched to `open -n --env` for the rest of the run.
- Window lookup with a small Swift helper that reads `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo`. The first version matched by owner name, which also caught other RepoOS processes. Matching by PID fixed it.
- Clicking through the Add server sheet with AppleScript `click at` coordinates derived from window bounds. This worked for the sheet, but not for the sign-in input.

## Challenges and blockers

The sign-in email field would not take input from synthetic events, which blocks the logged-in views. The test host also ran as a second Hub process during `xcodebuild test`, which may have written to the real registry because the test run did not set the isolated directory. I did not confirm that and did not check the real registry, so it stays an open question.

`xcodebuild test` left a `default.profraw` coverage file in the worktree root. I deleted it because it is a build artifact.

## Key learnings

A green build and unit suite do not prove the app works. The discovery and connect flow exercised real code paths that no unit test covered, and it passed. A blank-looking launch is not always a crash: the same bundle behaved differently depending on how it was started, so the launch method belongs in the record. The logged-in views still need a person, and the QA doc says so.
